transcript:
Header: 2025-03-19 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Maya Lin (Redwood CSM), Marco Sanchez (Lumenix), Elena Kim (Lumenix), Dave Rutherford (Lumenix), Sofia Alvarez (Lumenix)

Summary: Quick weekly sync for the Lumenix Private pilot. Reviewed perf numbers from last week after the partial kernel upgrade, discussed routing fallback behavior when peering flaps, validated patch for KV cache eviction, and agreed on next steps for a narrow canary rollback window and additional tracing. Some audio glitches; timestamps approximate.

Topics: perf review; VPC peering / transit routing; on-prem NAT/firewall rules; runtime 2.3 kernel/quantization patch; canary/fallback policy; security checklist (KMS & audit logs)

00:00 Speaker 1 (Jordan): All right hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll kick off. Quick agenda: numbers, networking, and then action items. Marco you on mobile or laptop?
00:06 Marco: Laptop, sorry had to hop from another standup — I can share my screen later if needed.
00:09 Jordan: Perfect. Priya do you want to lead the perf recap?
00:12 Priya: Yeah, sure. So we ran the 8k token demo workload from Wed through Sunday with the new kernel pins. Overall p50 improved ~8% and p99 showed ~12% improvement but we saw two small spikes on Thursday that correlated with peering flaps. The artifacts are in the spreadsheet (link shared in chat: https://redwood.app/pilots/lumenix-2025/benchmark-results).
00:35 Marco: Mm-hmm I saw that, the p99 was still a bit higher than we'd hoped at the heavy tail. What's the hypothesis?
00:40 Priya: Two things: one is kernel selection for long context still falling back to a slower attention kernel intermittently when the seq-length detection misfires; two is network queuing due to re-routing when transit peer changes. The kernel flip issue should be fixed in the micro patch we deployed yesterday but we need more run time to prove it.
01:05 Dave: Can you explain the kernel flip? Is that something on your side or our infra?
01:10 Priya: It's inside the runtime selection logic — when requests arrive with differing prefix lengths and the telemetry window is small, the runtime sometimes picks the conservative kernel which is higher latency. We pushed a guard that biases toward the optimized kernel when prefix cache hit rate is > 60%. That guard is in 2.3.1-alpha.
01:35 Elena: Are there any new security concerns with the alpha? We can't run anything with unknown crypto behavior.
01:40 Priya: No crypto changes. The alpha only touches kernel routing and quantization dispatch; KMS and keys are untouched. We'll push the exact diff to your security channel.
02:02 Marco: Okay good. Now networking — on Thursday we saw a BGP flap between the transit provider and our VPC that triggered the fallback to the dedicated public egress path and we lost some TLS warm caches which bumped latency. Sofia can summarize the firewall logs?
02:18 Sofia: yeah so the peer dropped and traffic rerouted over NAT Egress — we logged about 250ms extra per request during the interval. Traceroute showed an extra hop to the appliance. Also noticed a handful of connections reset because of strict TCP MSS handling on the appliance.
02:36 Jordan: So action there is getting the egress rules to allow path MTU to pass and relax the MSS clamp, and then tighten our BFD timers so reroute is quicker?
02:45 Sofia: yes and we want Redwood to validate that the fallback path preserves client IP headers for audit logs.
02:51 Priya: We do preserve X-Forwarded-For normally but when we fall back to the public egress we add a redwood-proxy header — that should still be fine for audit but Elena we can show you the raw logs.
03:08 Elena: Please do, we need to confirm no PII leakage and that the logs include request ids.
03:17 Jordan: Noted. We'll attach raw samples that have request ids and scrubbed payload.
03:21 Marco: On canary strategy — last week's canary pushed to 10% and we had one failing pod that triggered an auto-roll to previous revision which caused a small blip. How do we avoid a full rollout rollback?
03:31 Priya: Two recommendations: 1) enable connection draining grace longer for rollout windows (we suggested 90s) and 2) set fallback policy to route only new sessions to the canary, keep KV cache warmers pinned to stable nodes until warm. That reduces cold starts.
03:54 Dave: Warmers pinned — is that something we control? How do we pin warmers in our infra?
04:00 Priya: We provide an API to pin prefix cache shards to specific hosts in the pool; you can call that via your bootstrap. We'll share the script.
04:12 Marco: send that please. Also can you share the exact metric that triggered auto rollback? We want to tune threshold.
04:18 Jordan: It was error-rate > 1.2% sustained for 2m on the canary. We can lower sensitivity and use an extended evaluation window.
04:28 Marco: fine.

04:40 Speaker 3 (Maya): Quick note — the customer success plan suggests a dry-run rollback next week so everyone knows the steps.
04:45 Marco: Good idea. Put it in next steps.

04:50 Priya: Another smaller item — KV eviction: we observed faster eviction during heavy throughput which caused a higher miss-rate. We tuned eviction policy from LRU-approx to seglist with a soft TTL and it's better on our lab runs.
05:09 Sofia: Did that change affect memory footprint?
05:12 Priya: Slightly higher by ~3% but p99 latency improved due to fewer disk fallbacks.
05:20 Elena: On compliance: we still need the SOC2 artifact and the network diagram with the peering ACLs. Marco can you confirm what we already have?
05:28 Marco: We have the initial diag but not the updated peering ACLs. Elena will add a list.
05:33 Elena: I'll share ACL list and a mapping to Redwoods' egress IPs by Friday.

06:00 Jordan: Ok let's walk through the agreed live tests before next sync: 1) a 2-hour sustained throughput run with prefix caching on 2) a failover simulation where peering is de-provisioned for 3 minutes to validate fallback path 3) traceroute and tcpdump captures during the failover 4) security review of raw logs and KMS policies.
06:28 Marco: For the failover sim we want to schedule it during our maintenance window 03/27 06:00-08:00 UTC. Does that work for Redwood?
06:35 Jordan: Yes we can commit to that. We'll coordinate a dry-run on 03/26 with no traffic.
06:40 Sofia: we'll also run a synthetic load so you can see the tail.

07:00 Dave: small tangent, have you seen any issues with on-prem GPU drivers and the quantized kernels? We got a few OOM logs last week.
07:09 Priya: We noticed OOMs tied to older CUDA 11.4 drivers on the host. The runtime recommends 11.8+ for the new quantized path; we can add a guard to fall back to a lower memory footprint kernel if the environment reports older drivers.
07:30 Dave: plan on upgrading nodes to 11.8 in the canary before the full rollout.
07:35 Marco: okay. 

08:00 Jordan: Any other blockers?
08:04 Elena: just the KMS policy confirmation and the audit log samples.
08:08 Jordan: We'll upload an artifact zip to the shared drive with scrubbed logs and the kernel diff.
08:14 Priya: Also attaching the kernel selection debug flags you can enable for high-res traces.
08:20 Marco: cool.

08:30 Speaker 2 (Jordan): Recap / Next steps — Jordan reading: Redwood to send trimmed perf logs and p99 traces (Jordan) by 2025-03-20; Priya to share quantization profile + guard diff (Priya) by 2025-03-22; Sofia/Elena to confirm firewall ACLs and KMS policy (Lumenix) by 2025-03-21; Canary rollback dry-run scheduled 2025-03-26; Full failover sim 2025-03-27 06:00-08:00 UTC.

08:55 Marco: thanks everyone. Good sync.
09:00 Meeting ended.

References and artifacts mentioned: https://redwood.app/pilots/lumenix-2025/benchmark-results | kernel-diff.patch (attached in chat) | traceroute logs (to be uploaded) | SOC2 summary PDF (redwood-sec/soc2-2024-summary.pdf)
